backlog.spec: After the first SLSQP restart, keep the best packing. Each later iteration copies the best packing, picks 1 to 3 random circles, moves them to uniform random positions in [0,1]^2 with radius 0.01, then re-runs SLSQP from that perturbed state. Accept the result only if its repaired radius sum is higher than the incumbent. Use the same time budget as the current loop.
backlog.title: Monotonic basin hopping from incumbent

backlog.spec: Replace fresh random starts with perturbations of the current best centres. Add Gaussian noise with standard deviation sigma to every centre, where sigma starts at 0.05 and is multiplied by 0.97 after each rejected trial and reset to 0.05 after each accepted improvement. Clip centres to [0,1] and re-optimise with SLSQP.
backlog.title: Gaussian perturbation of incumbent with decaying step

backlog.spec: From the incumbent packing, delete the circle with the smallest radius. Find the largest empty hole by sampling 5000 random points in the square and choosing the one with maximum distance to all centres and to the boundary. Insert a circle there with radius equal to that distance, then run SLSQP. Keep the result only if the radius sum improves.
backlog.title: Remove-and-reinsert smallest circle

backlog.spec: Supply a jac argument to the SLSQP constraint dictionary and to the objective. For the pairwise distance constraints, fill the Jacobian analytically using the unit vector between centres and the pair index arrays; for boundary constraints use constant sparse-pattern derivatives. This removes finite-difference calls, which dominate run time, so more restarts fit in the 24 s budget.
backlog.title: Analytic Jacobian for SLSQP

backlog.spec: Only include the pair constraints for pairs whose initial centre distance is below 2*(0.25)+0.1, i.e. a neighbour list built once per restart. After each SLSQP solve, rebuild the list and re-solve once if any non-listed pair now overlaps. This shrinks the constraint vector from n(n-1)/2 to a few hundred entries and speeds each iteration.
backlog.title: Neighbour-list sparse pair constraints

backlog.spec: Set MAX_ITER to 1000 and pass options ftol=1e-12 to SLSQP so that restarts converge to a true local optimum rather than stopping early. Keep everything else unchanged. This tests whether the current 200-iteration cap is truncating useful progress.
backlog.title: Raise SLSQP iteration cap and tighten tolerance

backlog.spec: Alternate starting configurations: with probability 1/3 use a random perturbation of a hexagonal lattice that fits 32 or slightly more points in the square, with jitter of 0.02, choosing rows and offsets from the rng; otherwise use the uniform random start. Drop extra points by removing random ones. Seed all randomness from the seed argument.
backlog.title: Hexagonal-lattice and grid seeded starts

backlog.spec: Instead of setting every initial radius to 0.05, draw initial radii uniformly from [0.3, 1.0] times sqrt(0.7/(pi*n)), then let SLSQP optimise them. Mixed starting sizes encourage the optimiser to find configurations with unequal circles, which the target problem allows.
backlog.title: Random initial radii with area-based scale

backlog.spec: Replace the current _repair loop with a deterministic pass: first clip radii to the boundary distances, then repeatedly visit every violated pair and shrink only the smaller of the two radii to the amount that removes the overlap. Iterate over all pairs until no violation exceeds 1e-12. This loses less radius than rescaling both circles of the worst pair.
backlog.title: Exact feasibility repair by pairwise scaling

backlog.spec: Inside cons(), subtract a margin of 1e-9 from every pairwise and boundary inequality so that SLSQP returns a solution that is already strictly feasible. Then the repair step rarely needs to shrink radii, and the final SHRINK offset can be reduced to 1e-12. This recovers the radius sum lost in the repair stage.
backlog.title: Margin in constraints to avoid repair loss

backlog.spec: After the best packing is selected, run a polish pass. For each circle in turn, compute the largest radius increase allowed by the boundary and its neighbours (the minimum of the boundary gap and distance to each other circle minus its neighbour's radius), and apply it. Repeat the sweep until no circle grows by more than 1e-12. This is cheap and removes slack the SLSQP run left.
backlog.title: Final coordinate-wise radius growth

backlog.spec: For each restart, first minimise an unconstrained penalty function: negative radius sum plus weight * sum of squared positive overlaps and boundary violations, using L-BFGS-B. Increase weight through the sequence 10, 100, 1000, 1e4. Only then run SLSQP from the result. The penalty stage is smooth and fast, so the SLSQP stage starts closer to a feasible optimum.
backlog.title: Penalty continuation with L-BFGS before SLSQP

backlog.spec: Optimise a batch of 32 random configurations at once with a vectorised numpy penalty objective and a fixed-step gradient or Adam-style update on arrays of shape (batch, n, 2) and (batch, n). Run 2000 steps with penalty weight rising geometrically. Pick the top 4 by feasible radius sum and polish each with SLSQP. This uses vectorisation to explore many basins cheaply.
backlog.title: Batch of vectorised penalty starts

backlog.spec: Run 40 short SLSQP restarts with MAX_ITER set to 30. Keep the best 8 by repaired radius sum, then run each of them with MAX_ITER set to 300. Keep the best. Repeat the halving with the remaining time. This allocates compute to promising basins instead of giving every restart the same full budget.
backlog.title: Successive halving over restarts

backlog.spec: For each restart, first solve a problem where all radii are tied to one shared variable r, maximising n*r subject to the packing constraints. Use that solution as the start for the full problem with independent radii. Equal-radius starts often lie in a good basin, and the second stage lets the radii then relax into unequal sizes.
backlog.title: Equal-radius phase then free radii

backlog.spec: Treat each SLSQP local optimum as a state. Propose a new state by perturbing the current state (move one circle to a random location). Accept a worse state with probability exp(-(old_sum - new_sum)/T), with T starting at 0.01 and decaying geometrically to 1e-4 over the time budget. Keep the global best separately and return it.
backlog.title: Simulated annealing over basin-level acceptance

backlog.spec: In the basin hopping loop, choose how many circles to relocate at random from 1 to max(2, n//8) each iteration. Track the acceptance rate over the last 20 iterations and increase the number of relocated circles when acceptance is above 0.3 and decrease it when below 0.1. This keeps the search neither trapped nor too disruptive.
backlog.title: Adaptive perturbation strength

backlog.spec: From the incumbent, remove the k smallest circles, where k is chosen uniformly from 2 to 4 each iteration. Reinsert them one at a time at the points of a 2000-point random sample that maximise the distance to existing circles and boundaries. Then run SLSQP and accept only if the radius sum improves. This targets the weakest part of the packing.
backlog.title: Remove-and-reinsert the k smallest circles

backlog.spec: Build a 32-circle packing by starting from a good packing of 31 circles obtained by the same method. Add one circle at the largest hole found by sampling, then optimise all 32 with SLSQP. Start the chain from n=2 or from a random 4-circle packing and grow one circle at a time, keeping the best final configuration.
backlog.title: Incremental n-continuation from smaller packing

backlog.spec: Generate starting configurations that are symmetric under reflection about the vertical axis x=0.5 or the diagonal, by sampling half the circles and mirroring them. Make the mirrored circles share radii. Optimise the symmetric problem with SLSQP using half as many variables, then release the symmetry for a final unconstrained SLSQP run from that point.
backlog.title: Symmetry-constrained starts

backlog.spec: Run each SLSQP restart with a callback that records the radius sum. If after the first 30 iterations the sum is below the 40th percentile of previous restarts at that iteration count, stop the restart early and discard it. This saves time for more restarts without changing the final selection rule.
backlog.title: Early termination of unpromising restarts

backlog.spec: Sample initial centres with a beta distribution, Beta(0.8, 0.8), mapped to [0,1], so that starts place more circles near the edges and corners where large circles often sit. Keep the same SLSQP solver and repair step. This changes the initial distribution only.
backlog.title: Random restarts with a jittered boundary bias

backlog.spec: Add a small regularisation term to the SLSQP objective: minus radius sum plus lambda times the sum of squared radii, with lambda = 1e-3 for the first half of the iterations and 0 afterwards. The quadratic term pushes the first phase toward more even radii, which smooths the landscape and reduces early convergence to poor local optima.
backlog.title: Pair-distance penalty regularisation during SLSQP

backlog.spec: Add an L2 penalty on the deviation of centres from the square's centre (0.5, 0.5) with coefficient 1e-4 in the first SLSQP pass, then remove it for a final pass. This biases early configurations to fill the square evenly and avoids clustering in one corner.
backlog.title: Random restarts with weight decay on centre spread

backlog.spec: After the SLSQP restarts, take the best packing and run scipy.optimize.minimize with method trust-constr on the same constraints with a finite tolerance of 1e-10. Accept the polished result only if it passes the exact feasibility check and gives a larger radius sum. Use the remaining budget within the time limit.
backlog.title: Optimiser switch to trust-constr for final polish

backlog.spec: Within one call, after half the time budget, take the best packing found so far and generate new starts by copying it and jittering all centres with Gaussian noise of sd 0.02 and radii of sd 0.005. Run SLSQP from each of these, keeping the best. The deterministic seed controls all jitter draws.
backlog.title: Parallel-seeded perturbation of best packing across seeds

backlog.spec: Pass bounds to SLSQP directly instead of encoding them as inequality constraints: centres in [r_min, 1 - r_min] per coordinate and radii in [0, 0.5]. Remove the four boundary constraint blocks from cons(), keeping only pairwise overlaps. This reduces the constraint count from about 5n + n(n-1)/2 to n(n-1)/2 + n and typically speeds each SLSQP iteration.
backlog.title: Batch the boundary and radius bounds as variable bounds

backlog.spec: After SLSQP, linearise the radius-sum problem around the current packing and solve a linear program with scipy.optimize.linprog for increments to centres and radii, limited to a trust region of 1e-3. Accept the step only if the exact feasibility check passes and the sum improves. Repeat until no improvement is found. This gives a locally optimal, exactly feasible packing.
backlog.title: Growing-only radius polish with LP

backlog.spec: Measure the mean time of one SLSQP restart on the first two restarts. Choose MAX_ITER so that roughly 20 restarts fit in the budget, instead of a fixed 200 iterations. Recompute MAX_ITER after each restart based on the measured average time. This balances breadth of search against depth of convergence per restart.
backlog.title: Tempered restart count versus iteration budget

backlog.spec: In _solve_once, replace the uniform random start with a scrambled Halton sequence (bases 2 and 3) for centres, mapped into [INIT_LOW, 1-INIT_LOW]^2, with a random digit-permutation or shift drawn from rng so each restart differs. Keep the radii at INIT_RADIUS and the SLSQP call unchanged. Use Halton for about half the restarts and the existing uniform start for the rest, so the evenly spread starts are tried alongside random ones.
backlog.title: Halton low-discrepancy starts

backlog.spec: Build an initial centre set sequentially: start with one random point in the square, then repeatedly add the candidate point (sample 2000 uniform points from rng) that maximises its minimum distance to the existing centres and to the square boundary, until n centres are placed. Set each initial radius to half the distance to its nearest neighbour or boundary, capped at 0.1, then run SLSQP as usual. This gives a well-spread start that random sampling rarely produces.
backlog.title: Farthest-point greedy seeding

backlog.spec: Before the SLSQP stage, move the random start centres by minimising a Riesz repulsion energy sum over pairs of 1/(d_ij^2 + eps) plus a wall term that pushes centres away from the edges, using scipy L-BFGS-B on the centres only with the box [0,1]^2 as bounds. Run it for at most 200 iterations with eps = 1e-4, then set radii to the nearest-neighbour half-gap and call SLSQP on the full problem. This is a repulsion-based pre-spread that is distinct from penalty continuation.
backlog.title: Riesz-energy pre-spreading before SLSQP

backlog.spec: Replace the SLSQP call with an augmented Lagrangian loop. Treat the boundary constraints as variable bounds passed to L-BFGS-B (centres in [r, 1-r] is not separable, so use centres in [0,1] and radii in [0, 0.5]). Keep only the pairwise non-overlap constraints as penalised terms: L = -sum(r) + sum_ij (mu/2) * max(0, lambda_ij/mu + g_ij)^2 with g_ij = r_i + r_j - d_ij, and update lambda_ij = max(0, lambda_ij + mu*g_ij) after each outer step. Run 6 outer steps with mu starting at 10 and multiplied by 3 each step, then finish with a short SLSQP polish from the result.
backlog.title: Augmented Lagrangian with exact box bounds

backlog.spec: After SLSQP returns, find the active contacts: pairs with gap r_i + r_j - d_ij below 1e-6 and walls where the circle touches the boundary within 1e-6. Treat these as equalities and solve the resulting system for the centres and radii with a few Gauss-Newton steps (least-squares via numpy.linalg.lstsq on the Jacobian of the active constraints, objective sum of radii kept as a tie-breaker). Accept the Newton result only if all inequality constraints still hold within 1e-12 and the radius sum increases; otherwise keep the SLSQP result. Pass the final packing through the existing repair step.
backlog.title: Contact-graph Newton polish

backlog.spec: Each restart, first solve a packing of n+1 circles with SLSQP using the same random start scheme. Then, for each circle i of that packing, delete it, take the remaining n centres and radii as the start, and run SLSQP for n circles. Keep the best of these n+1 reduced packings as this restart's result. This reverses the usual growth direction, which removes the most constrained circle and lets the rest relax into a new arrangement. Budget the time so that the total stays under the TIME_FRACTION limit, and stop early if time runs out.
backlog.title: Reverse deletion from n+1 circles

backlog.spec: Keep an elite pool of the best 5 packings found so far, each with its (n,2) centres and radii. For a new start, pick two parents at random from the pool using rng, cut both at a random vertical line x = t in [0.3, 0.7], take the centres left of the cut from parent A and right of the cut from parent B, and fix the count to n by adding or removing the circles nearest the cut. Radii are set to the parent values for the copied circles and INIT_RADIUS for the rest. Run SLSQP on the child. Use this for about one third of the restarts after the first 20 percent of the time.
backlog.title: Crossover of elite packings

backlog.spec: Before SLSQP, run a few iterations of Lloyd relaxation on the random start: sample 4000 points uniformly in the square with rng, assign each sample to its nearest centre, move each centre to the mean of its samples, and clip to [INIT_LOW, 1-INIT_LOW]. Do 15 iterations. This spreads the centres into a centroidal-Voronoi-like layout. Set radii to the nearest-neighbour half-gap and continue with the existing SLSQP call.
backlog.title: Lloyd relaxation of centres before SLSQP

backlog.spec: Change the initial radii in _solve_once so they come from a two-size mixture: draw a random fraction f from [0.2, 0.6] of circles as large (initial radius 0.09) and the rest as small (initial radius 0.03), with the assignment chosen by rng. Keep the centre starts unchanged and run the existing SLSQP call. This tries starts with explicitly unequal circle sizes, which may lead SLSQP into a different family of contact graphs.
backlog.title: Bimodal radius starts

backlog.spec: Replace the linear objective -sum(r) in the SLSQP stage with -sum(r^p) and anneal the exponent p over three SLSQP calls: p = 0.5, then 0.8, then 1.0, each starting from the previous result. The power below 1 favours spreading radius across circles and avoids early locking into a single large-circle structure. Keep the constraints unchanged and reuse the same time budget, so the final stage is the standard linear objective.
backlog.title: Annealed power-mean objective

backlog.spec: Replace the non-overlap constraint sqrt(dx^2+dy^2) - r_i - r_j >= 0 in cons() with the polynomial form dx^2+dy^2 - (r_i+r_j)^2 >= 0, restricted to the case r_i+r_j>=0 (add the constraint r_i+r_j>=0 implicitly through the bounds r>=0). This removes the square-root non-smoothness at touching contacts, which SLSQP handles poorly. Run the same SLSQP call as before, then take the result and run a second SLSQP pass warm-started from it with MAX_ITER reset, keeping whichever run has the larger radius sum. Everything else (restarts, repair, time budget) stays unchanged.
backlog.title: Squared-distance smooth constraints with warm restart

backlog.spec: Rescale the decision vector so that centre coordinates and radii have comparable magnitudes: optimise u = (centres - 0.5) / 0.5 for coordinates and s = r / 0.1 for radii, with the objective -sum(s)*0.1 and the constraints written in terms of the unscaled quantities via the affine map. Unpack to true centres and radii before calling _repair. This is a pure conditioning change and should leave the optimum unchanged while making SLSQP's line search and finite-difference steps better scaled.
backlog.title: Variable scaling for SLSQP conditioning

backlog.spec: Add a third start type to _solve_once. Place about 4*sqrt(n) circles evenly along the four edges of the square at a small inset (for example 0.06 from each edge, with random phase per edge), then fill the remaining circles uniformly at random in the interior [0.15, 0.85]^2. Give boundary circles a slightly smaller initial radius than interior ones. Choose the start type with the seeded rng using probabilities roughly one third each for this, the hex start and the uniform start. The aim is to start from packings where the boundary is already saturated, which is typical of good solutions for this problem.
backlog.title: Boundary-first ring placement start

backlog.spec: Replace the fixed 6x7 hex template with a random lattice start. On each restart draw rows from {4,...,8} and cols from {4,...,8} using rng, build a rectangular or hexagonal-offset grid of rows*cols points spanning [0.08,0.92]^2, randomly delete or add points at random positions until exactly n centres remain (add uniform random points if too few, drop random points if too many), then add jitter of scale 0.02. This diversifies the lattice family across restarts instead of always using one arrangement, while keeping the seeded and time-bounded structure of solve().
backlog.title: Randomised lattice starts with varying row and column counts

backlog.spec: Before the SLSQP call, run a Lubachevsky-Stillinger style compression. Start n circles at random centres with radius 0 inside the square. Repeat for a fixed number of sweeps (for example 300): propose a random displacement of each centre of size about 0.05 times the current sweep-decaying scale, accept it only if the circle stays inside the square and does not overlap any other circle at its current radius, then grow every radius to the largest value that keeps all pairs and walls non-overlapping (min of wall distance and half the nearest-neighbour clearance, times a factor of 0.999 to avoid touching). Use the final centres and radii as the SLSQP start. Vectorise overlap checks with numpy. This is a bold, physics-inspired start that tends to produce jammed, well-spread configurations.
backlog.title: Monte Carlo compression of a hard-disc packing before SLSQP

backlog.spec: In each restart draw weights w_i uniform in [0.9, 1.1] for each circle using rng and minimise -sum(w_i * r_i) instead of -sum(r_i) in the SLSQP objective. The gradient is simply the weight vector on the radius block. Keep the reported score as the unweighted sum of radii after repair, so restarts are still compared fairly. Perturbed weights bias which circles grow first and steer SLSQP into different contact graphs, giving additional basin diversity without changing constraints.
backlog.title: Random per-circle objective weights to escape basins

backlog.spec: Maintain a small population (for example 8) of candidate centre sets within the time budget. Each generation, create offspring by taking a parent's centres and moving 2 to 4 randomly chosen circles to uniform random positions, plus a small Gaussian shake of all centres with scale 0.01. Run the SLSQP local solve plus repair on each offspring, and keep the top 8 by radius sum (elitist selection) for the next generation. Use the seeded rng for all choices and stop when the CPU budget is used. Return the best packing found. This is a population-based evolutionary strategy, distinct from single-incumbent perturbation.
backlog.title: Evolutionary search over centres with SLSQP as local solver

backlog.spec: After the first SLSQP pass in each restart, identify the smallest and largest circles and try swapping their centres while keeping each radius attached to its original index (so a big circle is moved to where a small one was). Accept the best of about 10 random such swap attempts only if a quick SLSQP re-solve from the swapped start yields a larger radius sum; otherwise keep the original. Swap moves rearrange the size hierarchy without changing the number of circles, which is a different neighbourhood from removing and reinserting one circle.
backlog.title: Swap moves between large and small circles

backlog.spec: Add a block-coordinate refinement after SLSQP. Fix the centres and solve a linear programme with scipy.optimize.linprog that maximises sum(r) subject to r_i >= 0, r_i <= wall distances, and r_i + r_j <= d_ij for pairs within a cutoff (for example d_ij < 0.35). Then, with radii fixed, take a few small gradient steps on the centres to increase the minimum pairwise clearance (for example maximising the minimum of d_ij - r_i - r_j via a softmin). Alternate these two steps 5 to 10 times, keeping the best valid packing after the repair step. This gives an exact radius optimum for each centre configuration and lets centres move between LP solves.
backlog.title: Alternating radius LP and centre relaxation

backlog.spec: Speed up each SLSQP solve by initially including only non-overlap constraints for pairs whose centres are closer than a random cutoff drawn from [0.25, 0.4] per restart. After the solve, compute all pairwise overlaps; if any pair in the full set is violated, add those pairs to the active set and re-solve from the current point. Repeat until no violation remains or three rounds are used. This keeps each iteration cheaper so that more restarts fit in the time budget, while the final packing is checked against all pairs before repair.
backlog.title: Per-restart random subset of constraints with full verification

incumbent.description: Fix the ValueError in _solve_once by flattening the pts array before concatenation so that all components have the same number of dimensions.

memo:
Helped: only slot 14, which fixed the hex/grid-seeded starts (-2.9309 and -2.9323, delta -0.0063, accepted). Incumbent is -2.9316 over 2 runs. Structured, diversified starts look like the useful direction.

Possible gains, not yet confirmed: slot 29 (power-mean objective with annealed p) scored -2.9358 and -2.9377 over 2 runs, but it was rejected at delta -0.0051. Slot 22 (perturbing the best packing) scored -2.9344, delta -0.0028, from one run. Slot 36 (Lloyd relaxation) scored -2.9338, delta -0.0022.

Did not help: two-phase refinement (-2.9223), L-BFGS-B penalty continuation (-2.9107, worst), remove-and-reinsert (-2.9227) and simulated annealing (-2.9238). Polish, adaptive MAX_ITER, Beta centres and density-based radii were within noise (sd about 0.0034).

Process: 17 slots failed with engine:patch_fail, 3 were aborted and 4 crashed. Use small SEARCH blocks copied exactly from train.py, each matching once.

Next: re-check slot 29, since it has 2 runs and the best scores, and replicate slot 22. Then try combining the power-mean objective with perturbation and Lloyd starts. Replicate before accepting.
